_about: B2 소르그림의 방패 — 카드별 장면 지시. 쓰는 법은 tools/art/PROMPT_GUIDE.md, 검사는 node tools/art/scene_tool.js lint B2.

B2-01.scene: Looking down from a gantry onto the curved back-plate of an unfinished golem laid flat on trestles: at the left a small woodpecker with a beak of blued steel clings to the plate with its back to us, head drawn far back over the next rivet in a long gleaming row. A chalk line runs beside the row, and a chalk tick marks where yesterday's work ended, well short of today's. A bucket of cherry-red rivets steams beside its claws, and a pair of tiny tongs lies ready.
B2-01.light: A single hanging oil lamp pools warm light on the plate around it; the workshop beyond falls away into black, the hot rivets glowing small and red.

B2-02.scene: From just behind a palm-sized clockwork mouse, over its brass back and the big wind-up key still turning between its shoulders: it scurries leftward along a frosty window ledge that crosses the whole frame, gear-wheel teeth bared, glass-bead eyes fixed on what waits at the far left — a thick, calloused apprentice's forefinger, already wrapped in one linen bandage, held out and wavering. Tiny scratch marks and three dropped cog-teeth dot the ledge behind it, and snow presses against the panes.
B2-02.light: Flat white daylight through the snowed-up window, cool and even, with soft grey shadows and a clean glint on brass key and steel teeth.

B2-05.scene: Straight down from the roof of an underground hall: a young pangolin apprentice whose scales still shine copper-bright stands in the middle of a tight ring of five old iron-grey pangolin smiths who all lean inward, sniffing at him, their long tapered snouts pointing at him like spokes that fill the frame. He tilts his narrow face straight up toward us, into one thin shaft of daylight from a vent far above, and hugs a brand-new round shield polished so bright that it mirrors all five wrinkled snouts.
B2-05.light: One narrow shaft of pale daylight drops from the vent onto his face and the shield; the hall around is dark silver-grey, the shield returning cold bright reflections.

B2-06.scene: Up through the rusty bars of a drain grate set in a workshop doorstep: the iron slats stripe the foreground, and above them on the right a short, dented, empty suit of plate armour stoops, turned toward the right. Behind its visor slit there is only a faint ember glow. With two gauntlet fingers it lifts the tip of a visitor's long braided beard — the visitor is only boot soles and that beard entering from the right edge — and holds it up to the glow to inspect the braid clasp.
B2-06.light: Dim green-brown daylight from the doorway above; the rust-red ember inside the helm warms the beard tip and the edges of the grate bars.

B2-07.scene: Over the hunched shoulder and ore basket of a kneeling carrier in the dark foreground, we look up a short flight of rock steps: at the top of the frame a riveted tower shield stands on its own two stubby iron feet, braced and turned toward the right, its worn leather arm-straps dangling empty behind it. A slingstone has just burst against its face; in the fresh dent a bright new rivet is pushing up through the steel like a bud, and the shield is already tipping its top rim forward to slam down in answer.
B2-07.light: Cold blue-grey light from the pass on the right rakes across the shield face, picking each rivet out in a crisp white point; the carrier is a slate shadow.

B2-09.scene: In flat side view on a loading ramp: a waist-high golem of riveted plate, with a pot-bellied boiler for a chest and a tin smokestack on one shoulder, has stopped dead in mid-stride toward the right, one square foot still lifted, a tall stack of iron ingots balanced in its arms. From its whistle the last thread of steam droops and thins like a sigh, and the glow in its seams has dimmed to a dull line. Just ahead of its raised toe waits a full coal scuttle with the shovel standing in it.
B2-09.light: Blue-grey evening light in an open shed, cool and shadowless; the last steam catches a pale highlight, and the boiler seams keep only a faint dying orange.

B2-12.scene: Extreme close-up of two open ape palms held side by side in front of a bed of glowing coals: on the left the broad young hand of an apprentice, fringed with gunmetal-grey fur, on the right the larger, soot-grained hand of its old master. Each leathery palm carries the same ridge of yellow callus under the fingers and the same polished groove where a hammer haft sits; the young one's are still pink at the edges. A small plain hammer rests in the crook of the apprentice's thumb, and an iron ring gleams on its wrist.
B2-12.light: Coals behind push molten orange between the fingers and along the edges of both hands; a dim steel-grey light from the front shows the palms.

B2-15.scene: First person across a shop counter: on the right a broad one-eyed smith with slate-grey skin, a single round eye under a heavy brow and bare, burn-freckled forearms holds a finished sword blade out toward us, flat on two open palms. The steel is long cold, yet its edges blur with a fine tremor. Everything near it answers: water in a tin cup on the counter stands in tight rings, loose filings crawl in a line toward the blade, the thongs of his leather apron quiver, and our own reaching fingertips, entering at the bottom edge, hover an inch away.
B2-15.light: One oil lamp behind his shoulder makes a small warm pool on the counter; the humming blade carries a thin cold streak of steel-grey light along its length.

B2-16.scene: A long black puddle between mine-cart rails fills the centre of the frame, and in it, bright and sharp, hangs the reflection of what clings to the gallery roof above: a pony-sized clockwork spider sheathed in overlapping armour plates, its head toward the left, six spiked steel legs hooked into the rock while the front pair turn a roof bolt home. Its glass lens eyes glint. On the wet floor beside the puddle lie the things it has outlasted: a burnt-out lantern, a cold lunch pail and a folded blanket.
B2-16.light: A single miner's lamp left on a ledge at the right lights the roof warm amber; the puddle returns it as a clean bright image ringed by black water.

B2-17.scene: From far across a gorge at dusk: a long rampart of grey stone climbs the mountain's spine from the left, tower after tower, and simply stops at a bare crag on the right of the frame, its last course of masonry butting against raw rock. On that crag, small and perfectly still, stands a shaggy grey mountain goat facing left along the wall, its huge curled horns of dark raw iron heavier than its head. Orange-brown ore veins streak the cliff beneath its hooves, licked to a shine at goat height.
B2-17.light: Blue-grey dusk under a clearing sky; the last cold light catches the iron horns and the licked ore in hard pale highlights against slate rock.

B2-18.scene: Flat as a frieze, a street of the underground city in side view: at the left a polished bronze bull with a round riveted boiler for a belly, one glowing firebox door in its flank and a brass valve between its horns stands facing right, head low. Twin jets of steam have just burst from its nostrils, and along the street ahead every hanging lantern swings away from it — the nearest flung almost level, the next half as far, the far ones only beginning to stir. A dropped loaf rolls along the cobbles.
B2-18.light: The swinging street lanterns throw small warm pools that slide over black stone; bronze flanks and steam catch amber, the vault overhead stays dark.

B2-19.scene: The frame lurches sideways with the rebound: a great soot-black anvil on four stubby iron legs barrels toward us from the right, its horn lowered like a snout, the hammer-scarred face on its back still glowing orange. The sledgehammer that struck it a heartbeat ago is flying back the way it came — head spinning end over end toward the upper left, the ash haft snapped in two — and a fan of sparks follows it. An empty tree-stump base stands behind it with four snapped bolts.
B2-19.light: The hot face and the sparks light the dark workshop from the right in molten orange; gunmetal shadows cover the floor and the far wall.

B2-22.scene: Down from a balcony into a narrow lane of the underground city: along both sides run plank doors, and each one shows a splintered round hole where its lock used to be, the hinges gone too, so that several hang askew. At the bottom of the frame the culprit ambles toward the right — a bear-sized beast with a bull's head, a short trunk-like snout and fur of bristling needles, its hide studded with half-sunk nail heads — chewing, the hasp of a padlock still sticking out of the corner of its mouth.
B2-22.light: Lamps in wall brackets leave small warm circles down the dark lane; the needle fur glints steel-grey wherever a circle touches it.

B2-24.scene: Against a white snow-sky, a black shape crouches on the timber lintel of a mine mouth at the right of the frame, facing right: a gargoyle whose body is an open frame of iron girders, with folded bat wings of riveted sheet steel and a long hooked jaw. The sky shows straight through its hollow ribcage, and the wind is driving a stream of snow through the gaps between the ribs, bending into a long plume on the far side. Below, a small lantern-carrying figure walks out under it, collar up, taking it for carved stone.
B2-24.light: Overcast mountain daylight behind it, bright and flat; the gargoyle and the mine mouth are solid black, the blown snow a soft grey veil.

B2-25.scene: Dead-on and symmetrical at the end of a stone corridor: a golem of riveted steel plate stands square to us, so broad that its shoulders touch both walls and its bulk hides all but the curved rim of the round vault door behind it. Its square fists hang at its sides, each as big as an ore cart. Cobwebs run from its elbows to the door frame, grey dust lies deep on its feet, and across the dusty floor one fresh set of footprints comes halfway toward it, stops, and turns back.
B2-25.light: Cold grey light from a shaft behind the viewer falls evenly on its plates in blue-grey and white; two pale furnace points glow where its eyes sit.

B2-26.scene: A mountain ridge cut open in cross-section: along the top of the frame, on the grass line, a massive rhinoceros armoured in overlapping dark-red iron plates walks toward the left, its horn of twisted iron lowered. Below it the cut rock fills two-thirds of the picture, and through it run thick cables of dark-red ore laid side by side like the sinews of a buried forearm. Directly under each planted foot the cables have bunched and tightened, glowing dull orange; where the rhino has already passed they lie slack and dark again. Pebbles hop along the surface.
B2-26.light: Dusk above the ridge, gunmetal and dim; the only warmth is the orange flex inside the ore cables, lighting the cut rock from within.

B2-27.scene: Head and chest fill the right of the frame: a grizzled guardian lion-dog with one blunt horn on its brow looks off to the left, eyes narrowed under a dented helm, in rust-streaked plate. The picture is really its mane — an iron-grey fall of a dozen thick braids, and into every braid is plaited a keepsake of a blow it stopped: a snapped sword tip, a notched sliver of axe blade, a bent arrowhead, each brown or green with age. The newest shard, near its collar, is still bright. Behind its shoulder a slab of riveted gate stands shut.
B2-27.light: Dim grey light from an arrow slit on the left grazes the helm and the old blade shards, showing rust red and verdigris against steel grey.

B2-28.scene: First person, looking down at our own heavy boots on the wet stone of a pump-room floor: a sledgehammer lies where we swung it, sunk in a cracked flagstone, and from every side bright beads of liquid metal are rolling back inward, joining into rivulets that race between our feet. In the lower part of the frame they have already pooled into one mirror-bright mass that swells up toward us in a smooth wave, knee-high and rising, and in its curved face our own warped reflection stares back — helmet, lamp and raised empty hands.
B2-28.light: Our helmet lamp is the only light; the liquid metal throws it back as hard silver glare, and the room around is black and grey.

B2-30.scene: Camera on the ground among rust-red ore rubble on a bare ridge: across the upper part of the frame a huge wyvern sweeps past from right to left, barely a wing-beat above the rock, iron-scaled wings blotting half the sky, hind legs tucked tight against its belly. In passing it has hooked a boulder of ore from the outcrop with the steel barb of its tail and carries it off, all on the wing. A marmot, tiny beside one fallen scale as broad as a tabletop, flattens itself in the foreground stones.
B2-30.light: High overcast daylight, snow-white and even; the wyvern's underside is granite grey with rust streaks, its shadow a soft blur racing over the rubble.

B2-32.scene: From inside the dark gate tunnel of the underground city, looking out toward the daylight: the arch has been hacked far wider and taller than it was built — raw pale chisel scars, scaffolding and heaps of fresh rubble line both sides — and in the bright opening on the right the reason is coming in. A castle of stone battlements and iron plate walks toward us on four great piston legs, its corner turrets scraping the new arch and showering grit. Masons with barrows, ant-small by its feet, are still widening the far side.
B2-32.light: Snow-bright overcast daylight pours in through the gate behind the castle, turning it grey against white; the tunnel walls nearest us stay in shadow.

B2-33.scene: Seen through a row of three stone doorways, one behind another: each lintel has been broken upward in the same tall notch, the shape of a helmet crest, and rubble lies fresh on every threshold. Beyond the last doorway, at the left, the cause walks on toward the right — a giant suit of pale grey plate armour with a tower shield on its arm, empty inside, a cold glow in its visor, its helm brushing the vault. It holds itself perfectly upright. A steward carrying a lamp reaches only to its knee, and has to trot.
B2-33.light: Cold blue-grey light from high clerestory slits falls in bars across the doorways; the armour's bone-pale plates take crisp white highlights.

B2-34.scene: Tipped by the blast, the whole frame leans: at the right a steel colossus as tall as the cavern bends forward and breathes out toward the right, a furnace burning orange behind the grille of its chest. From vents along its jaw and shoulders a white flood of steam pours down and away, filling the chasm beside it to the brim. Cable-lift cars sway on their lines and vanish into the cloud one by one; on a ledge at its ankle, a row of miners the size of rivets hold their helmets on and lean into the gust.
B2-34.light: The chest furnace is the one strong light, molten orange through the grille and glowing inside the nearest steam; everything else is gunmetal and dim white.

B2-35.scene: At a visitor's eye level in a hall of finished golems: on the right an old elephant, back level with a giant's chest, ears sagging and hide deeply wrinkled, in a scarred leather apron, faces right and presses the soot-black tip of his trunk against the breastplate of a steel giant whose head rises out of frame. Down the long rank behind him every golem carries the same small round soot mark on its chest, at exactly his trunk's height — dozens of them, shrinking into the dark. A lantern and a pot of soot sit at his feet.
B2-35.light: His lantern on the floor makes a small warm pool around his feet and the nearest golem's shins; the rank of golems fades to steel-grey glints in the black hall.

B2-36.scene: Low on the flagstones of a mountain gate court: filling the left of the frame stands one colossal bronze foot, toes pointing right, the ankle above it crossed by a seam that glows faint orange and is pinned shut by a single nail whose head is as wide as a cartwheel. Green verdigris runs down from the nail like old tears. On the ground in front lies a litter of failed attempts — long pincers, a crowbar, a grappling hook, a toppled ladder — and every one has been dropped a good ten paces short.
B2-36.light: Dim overcast light in the court; the bronze is brown and green-blue with age, and the thin seam at the ankle is the only warm line.

B2-41.scene: One headlong run shown as four overlapping moments across the whole frame, left to right: the same knee-high brass doll with a round rivet-eyed head and an oversized wind-up key whirring in its back appears four times — sprinting, sprinting faster, arms flung out, and at the far right flat against a sheet-steel door with its key still spinning. The door already carries a neat row of doll-shaped dents at exactly that height. Shed cogs and one spring mark the floor along its track.
B2-41.light: A caged lamp above the door lights the right side warm amber; the earlier figures fade leftward into darkness with steel-grey glints on their keys.

B2-42.scene: Square-on, filling the frame: an upright press automaton stands facing us on thick piston legs, and its whole front is two slab-like pressing plates held apart like opened jaws, top and bottom, their inner faces glowing dull orange with heat. Stamped flat into those faces are the outlines of what it met earlier — a breastplate, a kettle helm, a wheel, a ladle. Between the plates a gear-cased core ticks, red-hot. On the floor ahead lies a wheelbarrow rolled out as thin as a tray.
B2-42.light: The plates and the core glow orange from within and light the scorched floor; the rest of its frame is dark gunmetal with heat shimmer above.

B2-43.scene: Straight overhead on a snowfield where an army has drawn up: ranks of helmets and spear points make a tight grey pattern over the whole frame, except at the centre, where they bend away to leave a perfect empty circle of white. In the middle of the circle one tall brass-and-steel automaton stands alone, arms at its sides, a red core ticking behind the open gears of its chest and thawing a small dark ring in the snow. The only tracks inside the circle are its own. Every nearby helmet is turned toward it.
B2-43.light: Flat white daylight after snowfall, shadows short and soft; the red core is the single warm point in a field of white and steel grey.

EP-B2-1.scene: Looking steeply down into a mountain pass during a blizzard: at the right the pass narrows to a slot between two rock walls, one cart wide, and the slot is plugged by a single curled ball of iron spikes the size of a boar — rivets and nails for spines, a wet black nose just showing. Snapped spear shafts and a bent sword stand stuck in it. Back from the plug, down every switchback to the left edge, an entire invading column has stalled: carts, banners, a grounded battering ram, hundreds of small figures stamping their feet.
EP-B2-1.light: Snow-white storm light with driving flakes; granite walls grey, the spiked ball a dark steel knot dusted white on its windward side.

EP-B2-2.scene: From behind the rust-brown, hunched back of a mining golem at the left of the frame — boiler stack between its shoulders, forearms ending in blunt steel breaker-heads still grey with quarry dust — we see what its blow has done. The line of tower shields before it has split along one clean fracture, exactly as a rock face splits: plates shearing in flat slabs, rivets spraying like gravel. The crack runs on past the steel, across the ground and up the cliff beyond, where a whole slab of mountain is starting to slide.
EP-B2-2.light: Dim dust-brown daylight; rust and green-blue stains on the golem's back, steel-grey shards catching light as they fly, the fresh crack pale in dark rock.

EP-B2-3.scene: Framed by a vast empty gateway in a mountain wall, seen from inside the city: the bare hinge pins on either jamb are thick as tree trunks, and the night wind now pours in through the hole. Out on the causeway beyond, dead centre, the gate itself is walking away from us — a steel colossus whose broad flat back is two riveted door-leaves with a drop-bar across them, a lit guardroom window in one shoulder. Far ahead a line of enemy torches wavers. On the threshold, small as nails, the gate watch stand in a row, cloaks streaming.
EP-B2-3.light: Blue-grey dusk outside under a hard clear sky; the gateway's inner edge is slate shadow, and one warm window glows in the colossus's shoulder.

PN-B2-C1.scene: A rust-water pool below a spoil tip, shown in cross-section: the orange surface line runs across the upper frame, and the cut shows cloudy red-brown water over a bed of silt strewn with dropped rivets. On the left a broad crab with a riveted iron shell faces left and reaches one heavy tong-like pincer for another rivet; the other pincer is pressing one into its own shell with a twist. The shell is studded in careful straight rows, front to back, with a single gap left to fill.
PN-B2-C1.light: Dull daylight filters down through rusty water, red-brown and dim; the rivet heads on the shell hold small steel-grey glints, green-blue weed at the edges.

PN-B2-C2.scene: From behind, at the mouth of a fresh round burrow bored into an ore face: deep in the tunnel the broad dark-furred rump and stub tail of a bulky mole recede from us, steel claws flinging grit back, and the hot steam of its breath rolls out along the roof toward the camera. At the rim of the burrow, entering from both sides of the frame, three pairs of frost-stiff mittened hands are held open to the warm draught. A tin of tea has been set on the burrow's lip to heat.
PN-B2-C2.light: One lantern on the ground glows warm amber through the steam; the surrounding rock is black with frost glints, the mole a dark shape in lit fog.

PN-B2-C3.scene: A tilted frame, caught between two beats: on the right a steel colossus whose arms are solid hammers from the elbow down — square heads as big as mine carts, their striking faces worn mirror-bright — twists toward the right. Its left hammer is still raised across its chest where it has just stopped a catapult stone, which is breaking apart against it; its right is already falling, a blur of grey, onto the siege engine below. A rope ladder and a tiny oil-can crew cling to its shin, mid-chore.
PN-B2-C3.light: Cold clear morning light from the left; blue-grey plate with crisp white glints on the worn hammer faces, slate shadow under its arms.

PN-B2-E.scene: The head and chest of a golem fill the frame, facing us, and every plate of it is polished to a perfect mirror. In the curved breastplate we see ourselves as its foes do — a small, warped line of spearmen on a narrow rock bridge, lamps raised, hesitating. But the smooth dome of its face reflects something else entirely, something absent from the cavern: one vast slit-pupilled eye with an iris of molten metal, scaled lids of steel around it, staring out as if it were still in front of the golem.
PN-B2-E.light: The spearmen's lamps are the only true light, returned as hard silver glare; the reflected eye glows by itself, pale gold in a monochrome mirror.

PN-B2-U1.scene: Over the broad left shoulder of a beaver shield-smith — wet red-brown fur, scorched leather apron — who fills the left of the frame: he holds his own round shield up before him toward the right, facing the glow of a furnace door. Its face is covered in dents, each hammered flat, in tidy rows like a tally. One blunt claw rests on the newest, where a broken arrowhead is still lodged. His wide flat tail, shod in a plate of dark iron, lies on the anvil beside him, and the next shield he has hammered cools on a hook.
PN-B2-U1.light: The furnace mouth on the right paints each dent with a molten orange rim; his shoulder and round ear are dark gunmetal shapes against it.

PN-B2-U2.scene: From low among the rubble, looking up: on the right the great domed back of a beetle looms like a boulder, its shell raw ore — rough grey rock seamed with veins of bright iron — as it faces away from us and gnaws at an exposed vein in the cliff. A miner's pickaxe has just bounced off the dome and hangs in the air above it, the steel point curled over and the haft splitting lengthwise. Around the beetle's feet lies a scatter of earlier tries: bent chisels, a snapped crowbar, one leather wrist brace.
PN-B2-U2.light: Cold daylight from a cleft above strikes the shell from the left, blue-grey rock with white sparks on the iron veins; the cliff behind is slate.

TK-B2-1.scene: At eye level in a workshop passage: a compact golem of riveted plate, hardly taller than a door, steps out of a wall alcove straight toward us, one foot already over the sill. The dust sheet that covered it is sliding off one shoulder, and the furnace seams of its chest are brightening from dull red to orange, section by section, as it wakes. Above the alcove an alarm bell is still swinging on its bracket, and the pull-chain beside it sways.
TK-B2-1.light: The waking seams throw molten orange across the alcove and the falling cloth; the passage around is dark gunmetal with a faint grey sheen.

TK-U-SCRAP.scene: Down among the bolts and broken plates of a scrapyard floor: on the right a newly assembled golem pushes itself up to sitting and turns its head toward the left. Every part of it comes from a different machine — one arm of green-stained bronze, the other of rusted steel with a different rivet pattern, a dented boiler chest, a head with one round eye-lens and one square. The hoist chain that lowered its last piece still hangs slack from its shoulder, and a first unsteady puff of steam leaves its neck.
TK-U-SCRAP.light: Dim grey light over the scrap heaps; rust red and verdigris on mismatched plates, one weak ember glow starting behind the round lens.

UN-B2.scene: From inside the hollow chest of a half-built golem tall as a watchtower, looking out through its open breast-hatch, whose rim of salvaged plates rings the picture. Leaning down toward us, its face alone filling the opening like a cliff, is a titan of an old golem — hand-hammered plates of uneven size, crooked rows of rivets big as shields, a boiler patched many times. Between two huge, careful fingertips it lowers a salvaged furnace-heart, still glowing, into the cavity where we sit. Behind it snow falls on a valley of fallen machines, each already missing a part.
UN-B2.light: Snow daylight blazes white behind the old titan, rimming its dented shoulders against the dark hatch; the heart in its fingers lights its face plates warm from below.

UN-B2-7.scene: Two dark shapes against the snow-white daylight in the mouth of a mountain gate, seen from inside: two square colossi stand at the far left and right of the frame, each tall as the gate tower beside it, joined collar to collar by one chain with links the size of wagons. A hurled boulder big as a house bursts on the left golem's shoulder. The chain has snapped taut and level, frost flying from its links, and the right golem digs its heels in and leans away, taking half the blow. A besieging army's spear points glitter around their ankles.
UN-B2-7.light: Hard white snow-light pours in through the gate behind them; golems and chain are blue-black steel, with a crisp silver edge along every link and rivet.

UP-B2-12.scene: At the anvil of the same forge, seen from below: a great ape with gunmetal-grey fur, the apprentice grown into a master, stands at the centre turned toward the right, fur gone silver at the brow and wrists, the same iron ring on one wrist, a scorched leather apron on its chest. One broad calloused hand holds a glowing blade on the anvil with tongs; the other brings a heavy hammer down, sparks bursting at the strike. On the rack behind hang three hammers of rising size, the small plain one first, and a young ape works the bellows.
UP-B2-12.light: The bed of coals behind pushes molten orange along its fur and the anvil's edge; dark gunmetal gloom fills the hall.

UP-B2-17.scene: From below on the scree, looking up: the same shaggy grey mountain goat stands square on the bare crag at the centre, head lowered toward us, grown as tall as a watchtower, his curled horns of dark raw iron wound to a full double turn and wider than his shoulders, a jagged ridge of ore along his brow like a crown. The grey stone rampart ends against his flank on the left as if he were its last tower, and behind his back, sheltered, a whole herd of goats with short iron horns stands in line along the ridge.
UP-B2-17.light: Blue-grey dusk under a clearing sky; the last cold light strikes hard pale highlights from the great iron horns against slate rock.

UP-B2-18.scene: Camera on the cobbles of the same underground street: the polished bronze bull comes straight toward us at the head of a herd, grown to fill the height of the street, head low, the brass valve shrieking between its horns, three firebox doors glowing in a row along its riveted boiler belly. One forehoof has just struck the ground in front of the lens — the cobbles jump, cracks run outward, and steam bursts from both nostrils along the walls. Behind its shoulders three smaller bronze bulls follow in file, and every hanging lantern swings wildly.
UP-B2-18.light: Swinging street lanterns throw small warm pools over black stone; bronze and steam catch amber, and the vault overhead stays dark.

UP-B2-22.scene: From low in a scrapyard of the same underground city, looking up: the iron-eater sits at the centre atop a half-devoured heap of gears, shields and gate hinges, turned toward the left, now the size of a wagon — the same bull's head and short trunk-like snout, needle fur grown long as swords, its hide plated with half-sunk shields, and a ring of bent sword blades standing up between its horns like a crown. An anchor chain disappears link by link into its jaws. Around the foot of the heap three small needle-furred young gather the fallen nails.
UP-B2-22.light: Lamps in wall brackets leave small warm circles in the dark; the needle fur and the crown of blades glint steel-grey where they touch.

UP-B2-24.scene: Standing before the same mine mouth in the snow, looking up: on the timber lintel at the top of the frame crouches the gargoyle of open iron girders, facing us, grown twice as broad, its bat wings of riveted sheet steel spread to roof the whole entrance, long hooked jaw lowered toward us. A great ring of keys hangs from its neck, and its claws hold up three heavy chains that bar a riveted steel gate set in the mine mouth beneath it. Snow blows through its hollow ribcage. A small miner waits below, lantern raised, cap in hand.
UP-B2-24.light: Overcast mountain daylight, snow-white and granite grey; the girders and chains are dark steel, with a dull gleam on the ring of keys.

CS-B2.scene: What is left of a spell, lying in the lower part of the frame on a stone floor: a disc of conjured light the size of a cartwheel, its ring of bright blades caught half-open like a shutter, has gone hard and grey as cooled slag and dropped where it hung. A black iron wedge is driven clean through its centre, struck so recently that it still rings — a fine dust jumps around it. Along the crack the last blue sparks leak out and die, and the blades nearest the wedge have already dulled to plain iron.
CS-B2.light: Cold blue-grey light from the dying sparks plays over the grey disc; the wedge is a hard black shape with one white glint on its struck head.

MB-02.scene: A great curved armour plate fills the frame, caught half-mended: across its left half every seam is drawn tight under bright new rivets; across its right half the seams still gape, rivet holes stand empty and one panel hangs by a corner. The mending is travelling rightward — a stream of rivets flies in from the left edge, each one seating itself in the next empty hole with a small star of sparks, and just ahead of the stream the loose panel is already swinging flat. Old rivets, sheared in two, drop away from the mended seams.
MB-02.light: Polished new rivet heads flash bright silver in a cold beam from above; the unmended half stays dull grey, and the sparks are small white stars.

MB-06.scene: First person, advancing across a frozen lake: along the far shore, across the upper part of the frame from end to end, stands a wall of tall iron plates planted edge to edge, each glowing from dull red at the foot to orange at the top, the air above it rippling. The ice has rotted back from it in a wide strip of open, steaming black water. Our own spear, thrust out ahead at the bottom of the frame, is glowing at the tip and beginning to droop like a candle, and the leather of our glove smokes.
MB-06.light: Grey dusk over the ice; the plate wall is the light source, pouring molten orange onto the steam, the black water and the sagging spear.

MB-08.scene: The seam between two thick armour plates, enormously magnified, runs across the middle of the frame: a row of slotted screw heads sits along it, and all of them are turning the last quarter-turn at once, by themselves, thin curls of bright swarf lifting from each slot. The seam has closed to a hairline. Against it presses a thread of violet-black smoke — a curse hunting for a way in — which flattens, splays into searching fingers and slides off the steel like water off wax.
MB-08.light: Warm lamplight from the upper left rakes low across the plates, raising every screw slot and curl of swarf; the smoke absorbs it, dull violet-black.

NB2-2.scene: Seen from directly above on trampled snow: a line of shield tops and helmets runs across the frame from edge to edge, shoulder to shoulder. At its centre one shield, plainly thicker and broader than the rest, has moved a full pace ahead of the line toward the top of the picture, and the two bootprints behind it are fresh. The shout that sent it shows on the ground — loose snow has been blown forward in nested arcs fanning out from the whole line, all converging on that one broad back like a hand pushing.
NB2-2.light: Flat white mountain daylight from directly above; the arcs in the snow show as faint blue-grey ridges, steel rims catching a dull sheen.

PS-B2-1.scene: A single steel gauntlet, closed in a fist, stands knuckles-down on a stone in the lower part of the frame where rusty run-off trickles from a culvert and across the stones. Everything else the water has touched is eaten orange and green — a chain, a row of nails, a fallen helmet flaking apart, a pick fused to its own hook. The red water parts around the gauntlet and rejoins beyond it; drops that land on its plates bead and roll away, and the steel is as clean and bright as the day it was made.
PS-B2-1.light: Dim overcast light in a drainage cut; rust red and verdigris everywhere in half-dark, and one clear silver-grey gleam on the gauntlet.

PS-B2-2.scene: A cross-section through a stone quenching pool: the waterline cuts the frame in half. Chains are lowering a great kite-shaped slab of worked steel straight down through its centre. Above the surface the slab still glows soft orange and shows a thick rounded rim and a bulging middle. Below the surface the same metal has turned dark blue-grey and changed its shape as it hardens — the rim drawn out to a keen edge, the bulge pressed flat and dense. At the line itself the water boils white, and strings of bubbles climb the submerged half.
PS-B2-2.light: Above the water, molten orange light on steam and chains; below, cold dark gunmetal water lit only by the boiling line and one pale edge.

RB2-1.scene: The held breath in a mine gallery: a rank of steel machines stands along the whole width of the frame, cropped at the shoulders so only their riveted chests and hanging hands show. In every chest, at the same instant, the furnace-heart has gone from orange to white, and hairline cracks are racing outward across each breastplate and up into the roof timbers. Dust begins to sift down, the lamps along the wall all swing the same way, and on the floor a brass command lever lies snapped off its post, its red wax seal broken.
RB2-1.light: Small warm lamps along the gallery wall are being overpowered by the white hearts, which throw every rivet and roof prop into hard relief against black.

RS-B2-1.scene: The instant of a single tap, close up: at the right of the frame the small square face of a hammer, coming straight down, has just touched one seam at the shoulder of a heavy, ornate suit of plate armour. That one touch is undoing the whole. Plates spring apart along every joint at once, rivets jump out in a ring, buckles fly open, and the cuirass, pauldron and gorget hang for a moment as separate pieces in the air, each still perfect, with clear gaps of daylight between them. A chalk cross marks the struck seam.
RS-B2-1.light: Cold clear light from the left; blue-grey steel with white highlights on each separating edge, and slate shadow in the gaps between the plates.

SB2-01.scene: Side-on across a snowy slope, the track of a charge runs the whole width of the frame from left to right: a straight trench ploughed through a drift, then a palisade with one clean gap smashed in it, then a field wall of stone with the same gap, stakes and stones still tumbling. At the right end the thing that made it is still going — a tight wedge of iron shoulders and pauldrons at a heavy jog, seen only as plate and steam, heads lost in the snow they throw up. Beyond them one more fence waits.
SB2-01.light: Overcast snow daylight, white and granite grey; the armoured wedge is dull steel inside a cloud of thrown powder snow.

SB2-02.scene: A mirror-polished round shield fills the frame face-on. Punched into it in a tight ring around the boss are eleven red-hot rivets, each driven up to its head, and around each one the bright steel has bloomed into concentric haloes of temper colour — straw, bronze, violet, blue — so the shield's face is a ring of ringed targets. A twelfth rivet is arriving at the top of the ring on a straight white thread of steam, a hand's width from the metal. Cracks join the earlier hits like wheel spokes, and the boss has begun to sag.
SB2-02.light: The shield reflects a dark hall in silver-grey; the rivets glow orange at their cores and tint the steel around them, the steam thread is white.

SB2-03.scene: Inside a cracked armour shell, looking out through the split: a jagged vertical crack runs up the middle of the frame, and through it we see a strip of battlefield — churned mud, a planted banner pole, falling arrows. A blinding white bead of weld is climbing the crack from the bottom, closing it like a seam being sewn; below the bead the steel is whole and cooling from yellow to red to grey, above it the gap still shows the fight. Sparks shower inward past us, and two arrowheads piercing the plate glow in the heat.
SB2-03.light: The weld bead is the light, blue-white and fierce, throwing the inner rivets into sharp relief; a slit of grey daylight shows through the crack above it.

SB2-06.scene: Flat on the ground beneath it, looking straight up: the underside of a huge iron pressing plate fills almost the whole frame and is coming down. Its face is a grid of bolt heads, scabbed with rust and green stains and polished bare in the middle from years of flattening ingots. Daylight survives only as a narrowing band around its four edges, where the great screw-posts rise at the corners and chains run off toward a team hauling outside. A spear propped upright under the plate is bowing, and a helmet beside it is already half its height.
SB2-06.light: A thin band of grey daylight around the plate's rim is the only light, grazing rust red and verdigris on the bolt heads as the dark closes.

US-B2-1.scene: Looking along the hammer from its butt end: we stand behind the last of a single file of square steel machines, each gripping the shoulders of the one ahead, plates locking edge to edge so the file becomes one straight beam running away from us up the frame. At the far end, high in the upper frame, the foremost machines have clenched together into a massive block — the head — hanging over a fortress's gate towers at the top of its swing. Dark-red seams light up in sequence along the beam, back to front, like a pulse.
US-B2-1.light: Storm dusk, gunmetal and dim; the orange-red pulse in the seams travels up the beam and gathers as a molten glow inside the raised head.

US-B2-2.scene: High across a valley, the whole mountain range in view: along the valley floor a column of square steel ranks advances toward the left, small as a line of stitches, every right foot down at the same instant. The mountains answer the step. From each peak along the skyline an identical plume of snow has let go together, a row of avalanches starting in unison; the ice of a frozen lake has cracked in straight parallel lines; and a flock of rooks has gone up from the pines in a single sheet. Foreground pebbles hover above their ledge.
US-B2-2.light: Bright overcast mountain daylight, snow white and granite grey; the column is a thread of dull steel, the avalanche plumes softly lit from above.

IB2-1.scene: Above a rutted haul road a drag chain is stretched taut across the frame, from a mired ore wagon to a winch, and spliced into its middle, dead centre, are two overlapping slabs of old armour plate joined by a single rivet. Its broad domed head carries a small angular rune, one stroke crossed by two. Everything else in the line is giving way: chain links pulled long and thin, a hook straightening, the wagon's towing ring drawn into an oval. The riveted seam stays tight as a closed eyelid, rust and green stains weeping around it.
IB2-1.light: Dim wet daylight at a mine mouth; red-brown rust and verdigris on plate and chain, and a dull steel shine on the rivet's rubbed dome.

IB2-2.scene: A single standard armour plate — a thick, gently curved rectangle of steel as long as a forearm, with a rolled edge and a row of rivet holes down each side — hangs on two short chains from an overhead rail at the right of a proving bay, backlit by a window. The oak beam that carries the rail bows visibly under the weight. The plate's face shows a tight cluster of shallow dimples, and on the flagstones beneath lies what made them: five crossbow bolts with their heads mashed flat. Identical plates wait racked in the shadows.
IB2-2.light: Cold daylight from a high window behind the plate outlines its edges in crisp white; the face is blue-grey, each dimple holding a small slate shadow.

IB2-4.scene: A cutaway of a fist-sized drum of brass and steel, opened like a halved fruit, stands centred on a sheet of polished steel that doubles it in reflection. At its centre sits a sealed capsule of smoked glass holding one steady ember. Around the capsule turn three nested cages of fine gear wheels on spring arms, each ring able to give a little. The outermost ring has taken a blow: on one side its teeth are sheared and a spring is bent, the next ring has shifted a hair, and the capsule at the heart sits perfectly true.
IB2-4.light: Bright silver-grey reflections on every gear tooth and on the mirror plate beneath; the ember adds one small warm point at the centre of a dark room.

IB2-5.scene: Planted upright on a timber post at the right, where a snow-covered stair reaches a mountain gate, stands a shield that used to be the palm of a giant machine's hand: a thick, cupped slab of dark iron taller than a door, the stubs of four finger knuckles along its top edge and a thumb joint at one side, old palm-creases showing as riveted seams. Fingers up, it faces down the stair like a hand raised to say halt. A grip of forged bar is bolted where the wrist was. Two spent arrows lie at the foot of the post.
IB2-5.light: Flat white daylight under low cloud; the iron is granite grey with a pale steel sheen on the knuckle stubs, snow bright all around.

IB2-6.scene: In a rock-wall niche at the centre of the frame sits the core of a giant machine, laid on a folded soot-black apron: a sphere the size of a pumpkin, banded with dark iron hoops and riveted straps, a round port of thick glass in its face behind which a slow orange glow turns. The hoops are scored where great tongs gripped it. Along the ledge in front, offerings have been set out in a row — cups of lamp oil, three lumps of coal, a worn rasp, a braid of grey beard tied with wire.
IB2-6.light: Two small oil flames on the ledge and the core's own slow glow make a warm pool in the niche; the hall beyond is black with steel-grey glints.

M3-1.scene: Half made: a loaf-sized block of dark iron, a machine's heart, sits clamped in a screw-jig at the centre of a stone bench, and a single angular rune is being cut down into its top face. The left half of the mark is finished, a deep channel filled with molten orange light; the right half is only a scribed white line. A narrow chisel stands upright in the groove where the cutting stopped, its head mushroomed from blows, curls of bright iron around it. Beside the jig sits an uncut blank from the same bar, shrivelled to walnut size.
M3-1.light: The cut half of the rune glows molten orange and lights the chisel and the jig from below; the bench around is dark gunmetal.

PI-B2.scene: At the left of the frame, on a ledge of an exposed ore face at nightfall, lies a coil of cable as thick as a wrist — dark-red iron fibres twisted like the strands of a tendon, wound in three loops with its free end pointing left. Beside it the cliff shows its source: a vein of the same dark-red ore, bared like a sinew, ending in a clean cut stub with the identical twisted grain. The coil glows dull orange from within. It has burned through its sledge, and the heather around has caught fire.
PI-B2.light: Blue-black nightfall on the mountain; the coil's orange heat lights the cut vein, the charred sledge and the small flames in the heather.

IR-B2.scene: Caught in mid-air at the right of the frame: a sheet of dull grey metal the size of a breastplate and thin as a roofing slate shoots flat out of a rolling-mill shed toward the right, over a snowy yard, a shimmer of vibration along its raw edge. Behind it the mill tells the rest: the two great steel rollers it has just passed between are scored with deep grooves, and the lower one has cracked clean across, its halves sagging while a snapped drive-chain whips loose. The sheet itself is flawless, cold and matte.
IR-B2.light: Overcast snow daylight, white and even; the grey sheet is crisp against the snow, the cracked rollers dim inside the granite-dark shed.

NB2-1.scene: In side view along the bottom of the frame, three boiler-driven golems charge to the right across an iron bridge, each dragging a long level streak of steam ripped from every seam. Their whistle valves are lashed shut with chain, rivet heads glow cherry-red, and the shaking has thrown the rust off them in clouds of red-brown flakes that hang along the whole run. The lightest frame comes last, the middling one ahead of it, and far out in front, buckling the deck plates at each stride, pounds the heaviest: a slab-sided hulk of doubled plate.
NB2-1.light: Dim storm daylight over a chasm; rust-red flakes and green-stained copper pipes against steel grey, the steam streaks pale and the rivets small hot points.

PN-B2-R.scene: A locked shield wall fills the frame from edge to edge — one rank kneeling, one standing, a third held overhead — round steel shields overlapping like scales, all tilted toward the left. In the left third a spirit holds one place in the line: translucent steel plates hanging in the shape of one huge raised forearm, elbow at the ground, fist above the helmets, a faint forge-glow at its core. The shields nearest it have taken on its sheen, dents smoothed and rims doubled by a ghostly second edge, the polish fading shield by shield toward the right.
PN-B2-R.light: Hard silver light from a white sky is mirrored in every polished boss; the dark pass shows only as reflections, the spirit's core one small warm point.

RS-B2-2.scene: On a snowy saddle between two peaks, seen from high behind: at the left a rank of square iron golems stands shoulder plate locked to shoulder plate, facing left into a cold white glare of hostile spell-light. Their joined shadow is the subject. It falls to the right across the snow as one solid band, sealed from end to end, with a jagged top like a mountain ridge; inside it the snow lies clean and blue, tents stand, a watch-fire burns upright. Beyond the shadow's two ends the snow is scorched grey and the heather smokes.
RS-B2-2.light: A harsh white glare from the left edge under a slate-blue dusk; the shadow band is cool blue-grey, and every steel shoulder carries a crisp white rim.

RS-B2-3.scene: Red-hot rivets fill the frame from edge to edge, thousands of them, flying leftward in slanting streaks like driven sleet. At the right edge the spilled hoppers of overturned riveting engines still pour them out. Midway the storm crosses a rack of plain square breastplates, and there the rivets seat themselves with small flashes, heads lining up in neat new rows along every seam. At the far left it meets a line of black spiked shields and goes straight through, leaving each one stitched with round holes that let the furnace glow shine out behind.
RS-B2-3.light: Gunmetal gloom of a forge yard at night; the rivets are the light, orange-white streaks that stay glowing in the new seams and in every punched hole.

RS-B2-4.scene: A steep stair cut into a mountain pass runs down the left of the frame, and a column of locked tower shields comes down it straight at us, rank stacked above rank like a pillar of steel. Every rank leans forward at the same slant, each shield pressed flat on the backs below, so the weight of the whole stair bears down on the one great shield at the bottom, huge in the foreground. Its boss has just struck a timber barricade: logs burst apart, and grit and rainwater leap off every step at once.
RS-B2-4.light: Dim storm light in the pass; rust-streaked shields with verdigris-green bosses, the splintered timber pale against wet dark rock.

SB2-09.scene: Framed by the timber props of a mine gallery's mouth, high in a vast cavern's wall: the whole underground city lies below, level under level, and every furnace in it is lit — hundreds of small orange doors glowing in the black, a hammer rising and falling in each pool of light. In the left of the frame the great shaft climbs toward the surface, and up it, away from us, moves an endless chain of lift cradles, each carrying a freshly riveted shield or breastplate, dull red at the edges, toward a far bright gate.
SB2-09.light: Black cavern dark holding hundreds of small warm furnace mouths; steel glints at the edge of each pool and all along the moving lift chain.

SP-B2.scene: Side view inside a forge hall hollowed from a sleeping giant's arm: the back wall is that forearm, raw iron ore banded with bright sinews thick as bridges. One sinew has been drawn out white-hot like a cable into the open chest of a colossus of white steel standing on the right, facing left — there it ends in a heart of silver valves and pistons striking its first beat. The colossus raises a hammer broad as a bridge pier. Along a quenching pool at its feet kneel golems small as its toes, their eye-lamps opening in a wave.
SP-B2.light: The heart's silver-white blaze and the glowing sinew light the hall, flashing on white steel and steam; each beat sends one bright ring across the black water.

SR-B2.scene: Glimpsed through a reliquary grille whose bars are swords — every one bent back double on itself at the same place — set upright across the foreground. Between them, low in the frame on a block of raw iron ore, rests a cuirass that was grown rather than forged: one hollow knuckle of a colossal rib, grey bone-metal with natural flanges curving round like shoulder guards, two plain leather straps its only made parts, its breast turned toward the right. Its surface is smooth and bright enough to mirror the bent blades.
SR-B2.light: A cold shaft of daylight from a slot in the rock strikes the breast, which answers with a brightness of its own, casting silver reflections across the bent blades and the raw ore.
